primary-onyx.displayName: Primary Onyx (ink/paper inversion — never a fixed hex)

selected.displayName: Selected — the only 'this is the active choice' color

cover-gold.displayName: Cover Gold (book-object only — never UI chrome)

display.purpose: Screen-level titles; engraved, wide-tracked bookplate/spine-lettering feel. 48px / 32px mobile, 0.08em tracking.

headline.purpose: Section headers within a screen (.section-title). 24px, 0.05em tracking.

title-sm.purpose: Compact display titles on small surfaces — book-cover placeholder titles, drawer/sheet titles. 15px, 0.06em tracking.

reading.purpose: Chapter body text inside the reader iframe. 20px / 17px, 1.6 line-height, max 68ch.

reading-lora.purpose: Book text only, chosen in Settings / reader toolbar. Applied via --reading-font-family inside the iframe. Not a UI font.

reading-dm-sans.purpose: Book text only. Same application path as Lora; never used for app chrome.

reading-atkinson.purpose: Book text only. Disambiguates similar characters for low-vision readers.

ui.purpose: Buttons, nav, controls, labels. Deliberately neutral so it never competes with either serif. 14px / 12px small.

meta.purpose: Timestamps, byline-style metadata, badges, cover-placeholder author labels. 11px, 0.05em tracking.

mono.purpose: Code, data, measurement — never as a 'technical' costume.

shadows.name: soft
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation for book covers and card-like content surfaces (.elevated-soft) — a constant signature, not hover-only. Heavier alpha in dark mode.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Heavier lift reserved for elements that overlay other content directly (.shadow-floating).

motion.name: press-nudge
motion.purpose: Tactile 'pressed into the page' cue on buttons (active:translate-y-px).

motion.name: sheet-slide
motion.value: slide up from the bottom viewport edge
motion.purpose: Bottom sheets (TOC drawer, reader toolbar) enter from the edge rather than fading in — the elevation cue is border + rounded top + slide, not shadow.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation-duration: 1ms; transition-duration: 1ms; animation-iteration-count: 1; scroll-behavior: auto }
motion.purpose: Collapses motion to ~instant while keeping every final state and color-feedback change intact — the OS setting is the single source, there is no in-app motion toggle.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default call-to-action; modest tool-like rounding, solid ink fill that inverts with the theme.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--color-primary, #040505); color: var(--color-primary-foreground, #fff9ee); padding: 0 10px; height: 32px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0.225rem; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.15s, transform 0.1s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-primary, #040505) 80%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-ring, #695d4a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-ring, #695d4a) 50%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action — transparent fill, control-edge border (--input, not the decorative --border).
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: var(--color-foreground, #1f1c0f); padding: 0 10px; height: 28px; border: 1px solid var(--color-input, #7c7e7e); border-radius: 0.225rem; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--color-accent, #f2e0c8); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-ring, #695d4a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-ring, #695d4a) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Ghost Icon Button
components.description: Icon-only nav control in the sticky header (search, menu, overflow). Hit area ≥ 24px per WCAG 2.5.8.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--color-foreground, #1f1c0f); width: 28px; height: 28px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0.225rem; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--color-surface-high, #f0e8d4); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-ring, #695d4a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-ring, #695d4a) 50%, transparent); }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: The library search input — a filled parchment pill; focus lands on the container as a ring, not the bare input.
components.css: .ds-search { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 12px; background: var(--color-card, #f5edd9); border-radius: 0.3rem; color: var(--color-muted-foreground, #444748); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px transparent; transition: box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-search:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-ring, #695d4a) 50%, transparent); } .ds-search input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; border: none; background: transparent; outline: none; font-family: 'Literata', serif; font-size: 15px; color: var(--color-foreground, #1f1c0f); } .ds-search input::placeholder { color: var(--color-muted-foreground, #444748); }

components.name: Radio Row (selectable list row)
components.description: Full-row radio for named-option lists (theme selector, font selector) — the whole row is the target, with an inset ring when checked and a distinct focus ring.
components.html: Literata
components.css: .ds-radio-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 16px; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; outline: none; color: var(--color-foreground, #1f1c0f); font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; } .ds-radio-row:focus-visible { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--color-ring, #695d4a); } .ds-radio-row-checked { background: var(--color-surface-high, #f0e8d4); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px var(--color-selected, #835a00); color: var(--color-selected, #835a00); }

components.name: Book Card
components.description: Library grid item: rounded cover with a resting soft shadow that deepens on hover; NEW badge is a filled corner tab, not a floating chip.
components.css: .ds-book-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; } .ds-book-card-cover { position: relative; aspect-ratio: 2 / 3; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 0.525rem; border: 1px solid color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-border, #c4c7c7) 40%, transparent); box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(31,28,15,0.04); background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--color-cover-dark, #2b241c), var(--color-cover-gold, #c9a84c)); transition: box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-book-card-cover:hover { box-shadow: 0 8px 24px rgba(31,28,15,0.12); } .ds-book-card-badge { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; background: rgba(255,249,238,0.95); font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-muted-foreground, #444748); padding: 4px 10px; border-bottom-left-radius: 0.525rem; }

components.name: Bottom Sheet
components.description: TOC drawer / reader toolbar: slides up from the viewport edge, rounded top corners only, a hard top border instead of a shadow. List items are Button variants — they keep the modest control radius even inside the generously rounded sheet.
components.css: .ds-sheet { display: flex; flex-direction: column; max-height: 85dvh; background: var(--color-card, #f5edd9); border-radius: 0.825rem 0.825rem 0 0; border-top: 1px solid var(--color-divider, #eae2ce); } .ds-sheet-handle { width: 64px; height: 4px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-border, #c4c7c7); margin: 12px auto 16px; } .ds-sheet-header { font-family: 'Cinzel', serif; font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 0 24px 20px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-divider, #eae2ce); } .ds-sheet-item { text-align: left; padding: 8px 24px; border: none; border-radius: 0.225rem; background: transparent; font-family: 'Plus Jakarta Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-foreground, #1f1c0f); } .ds-sheet-item:hover { background: var(--color-surface-high, #f0e8d4); } .ds-sheet-item-active { background: var(--color-secondary, #f2e0c8); color: var(--color-secondary-foreground, #695d4a); }

components.name: Sticky Header
components.description: Translucent blurred header with hairline top/bottom dividers; content scrolls beneath it without a hard seam. Icon-only ghost controls, no text labels.
components.html: Librune
components.css: .ds-header { position: sticky; top: 0; height: 80px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 8px 20px; background: var(--color-header-bg, rgba(255,249,238,0.85)); backdrop-filter: blur(12px); border-top: 0.5px solid var(--color-divider, #eae2ce); border-bottom: 0.5px solid var(--color-divider, #eae2ce); } .ds-header-title { font-family: 'Cinzel', serif; letter-spacing: 0.08em; font-size: 20px; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-foreground, #1f1c0f); }

narrative.overview:
Librune reads like a physical folio: warm cream paper, an ink-black spine of UI chrome, and a gold-on-dark cover accent that echoes traditional bookbinding. The reading surface is set in serif type on soft parchment tones, while the architectural chrome around it — buttons, toolbars, the sticky header — stays quiet and disciplined, so it never competes with the page. Book covers, bottom sheets, and panels are the "paper objects" of the system: they get more generous rounded corners and a consistent gentle lift, as if resting slightly above the surface beneath them. Depth is soft and consistent rather than occasional — every card-like surface carries the same low ambient shadow at rest, not just on hover, reinforcing the sense of physical layered pages.

Corners are soft everywhere, but graduated by role rather than uniform: controls (buttons, menus, dialogs) take a small, disciplined radius that keeps them feeling like precise tools; content objects (book covers, bottom sheets) take a larger radius that reads as a physically rounded paper object. The split is in degree, not in kind — nothing in the system is hard-edged.
keyCharacteristics: Warm parchment palette in light mode, near-black ink in dark mode — never a cold neutral gray.
Serif display (Cinzel, wide letter-spacing) for titles; serif body (Literata) for reading; sans (Plus Jakarta Sans) for UI chrome only.
Softly rounded throughout, graduated by role: controls (buttons, menus: rounded-sm) read as precise tools; content objects (covers, sheets: rounded-xl / rounded-3xl) read as rounded paper.
Consistent soft ambient shadow as a resting-state signature, not just a hover effect.

rules.name: The Boundary vs Decoration Rule
rules.body: --input is every control boundary (outline-button edges, switch off-track, radio outlines, the search underline) and is held at 3:1 against every surface it sits on. --border / --divider are decorative container edges and stay soft on purpose. Never use border-border on something the user clicks; never darken --border to fix a control's legibility.

rules.name: The Cover Accent Rule
rules.body: cover-dark and cover-gold are reserved for book-cover placeholder gradients and never used as UI chrome colors — they signal 'this is a book object', not 'this is a control'.

rules.name: The Ink Inversion Rule
rules.body: Primary is never a fixed hex — always the current theme's ink-on-paper extreme (near-black on cream, near-white on near-black). Use the --primary token so dark mode inverts correctly.

rules.name: The Selection Accent Rule
rules.body: selected is the only color that means 'this is the active choice' — it must not be reused for hover states, emphasis, or decoration, or the signal dilutes. It is a deliberately different hue relationship from cover-gold so the two never get confused.

rules.name: The Ramp-Only Rule
rules.body: Every font size comes from the --text-* scale (text-display-lg through text-meta) — never Tailwind's built-in text-sm / text-base / text-xs, even in shadcn-generated primitives, and never a literal px value.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Content Rule
rules.body: Any text the reader is meant to actually read (titles, chapter text) uses a serif; any text that helps them operate the app (buttons, nav, meta labels) uses the sans. Don't cross the two.

rules.name: The Resting Lift Rule
rules.body: Content objects (book covers) carry .elevated-soft at rest, not only on hover — depth communicates 'this is a physical object', not 'this is interactive'.

rules.name: The Object/Control Split
rules.body: If it's something the user reads or holds (a book cover, a sheet, a popover), round it generously (rounded-xl / rounded-3xl). If it's something the user presses (a button, a menu, a dialog), round it modestly (rounded-sm). Both are always softly rounded — the split is in degree, not sharp-vs-round.

dos: Do keep controls at the modest end of the radius scale (rounded-sm) — never sharp, never as generous as a content object's radius.
Do give content objects (covers, sheets) a rounded, soft-lifted treatment (.elevated-soft + rounded-xl / rounded-3xl).
Do pair serif type (Cinzel / Literata) with anything the user reads, and sans (Plus Jakarta Sans) with anything the user operates.
Do use the --primary token (never a hardcoded hex) for anything meant to invert correctly between light and dark mode.
Do reserve cover-dark / cover-gold strictly for book-cover-related surfaces.
Do use selected only to mark active/checked state (switches, radio rows, active-filter indicator) — never as a hover tint or decoration.
donts: Don't round a button or chip to match a content object's larger radius — it breaks the control/content split.
Don't add a drop shadow to bottom sheets; their elevation cue is the top border + rounded-top-corners + slide animation, not shadow.
Don't introduce a cold neutral gray; all neutrals in this system are warm parchment/ink tones.
Don't use the sans UI font for reading-surface body text, or the serif reading font for buttons/nav labels.
Don't use warm-accent or selected interchangeably with cover-gold — they're deliberately distinct hues so 'book object', 'CTA tile', and 'active selection' stay three separate signals.
